name: Brainwallets
mechanism: private key = SHA-256 of a human phrase; phrases from books, songs and leaks swept by bots within seconds

name: Randstorm (BitcoinJS)
mechanism: wallets created 2011–2015 drew keys from the browser's Math.random() behind JSBN's SecureRandom()
amount: ≈ 1.4 M BTC estimated in possibly weak wallets (Unciphered), not stolen

name: Profanity → Wintermute
mechanism: vanity generator expanded 256-bit keys from a 32-bit seed; an admin address made with it was recovered

name: Trust Wallet extension
mechanism: Mersenne Twister mt19937 seeded with 32 bits (versions 0.0.172–0.0.182); exploited Dec 2022 and Mar 2023

name: Milk Sad (Libbitcoin Explorer)
mechanism: bx seed used mt19937 seeded with 32 bits (versions 3.0.0–3.6.0); exploited June–July 2023

name: Coldcard hardware wallets
mechanism: #ifndef instead of #if ! let seed generation link MicroPython's Yasmarang PRNG (chip ID ⊕ timer) instead of the hardware TRNG, 2021–2026
source: Coinkite security advisory (30 Jul 2026); Wizardsardine; note 09

name: Sony PS3 firmware signing
mechanism: ECDSA with a constant nonce: two signatures gave the signing key (fail0verflow)

name: Android SecureRandom
mechanism: a broken system generator made Bitcoin wallets repeat ECDSA nonces

name: Biased Nonce Sense
mechanism: a few predictable nonce bits over many signatures: lattice attacks recovered hundreds of real keys

name: Slope wallet (Solana)
mechanism: the mobile app sent seed phrases to a Sentry logging server, stored readable

name: Ronin bridge
mechanism: attackers gained enough validator signing keys through a compromised node and social engineering

name: The DAO
mechanism: reentrancy: Ether was sent before the balance was updated, so withdraw was re-entered

name: Parity multisig
mechanism: July: unprotected initialisation (≈ 150 000 ETH stolen). November: the shared library self-destructed (≈ 514 000 ETH frozen)

name: BadgerDAO
mechanism: a compromised Cloudflare API key injected a script asking users for unlimited token approvals

name: Ledger Connect Kit
mechanism: a phished former employee's account published malicious npm versions 1.1.5–1.1.7: a wallet drainer in every DApp using it, ≈ 5 h

name: Bybit
mechanism: malicious JavaScript in Safe{Wallet}'s S3 bucket altered Bybit's cold-wallet transaction during signing
amount: ≈ $1.5 B, the largest crypto theft to date

name: Address poisoning
mechanism: a look-alike address matching the first and last characters, planted in the victim's history, then copy-pasted

name: Clipboard hijacking
mechanism: malware replaces a copied address with a look-alike
